organism.scientificName: Mycoplasmoides genitalium (strain ATCC 33530 / DSM 19775 / NCTC 10195 / G37)

texts.value: Part of the major adhesin Nap complex which mediates attachment to host ciliated epithelium (PubMed:17028283). This protein and P110 (mgpC) mutually stabilize each other, and are required for formation of the attachment organelle (PubMed:17028283). The P140-P110 Nap complex plays a major role in motility (PubMed:26712501, PubMed:29470847). The attachment organelle is involved in gliding cell motility and adhesion to host cells (PubMed:17028283, PubMed:29470847). One possible human receptor for this protein is peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase A (cyclophilin A, PPIA) (PubMed:29551599). Stimulates PPIA/CYPA secretion by human urothelium cell line (SV-HUC-1) (PubMed:33013867)

Part of Nap adhesion complex, which consists of 2 P140(mgpB)-P110(mgpC) heterodimers (PubMed:28671286, PubMed:32513917, PubMed:37939157). The interaction interface between P140 and P110 near the cell surface is critical for motility (PubMed:32513917). Interacts with human PPIA/CYPA in solution and on the surface of a human urothelium cell line (SV-HUC-1); shown with residues 1075-1444 (PubMed:29551599)
Localizes over the Nap region, a differentiated covering of the attachment or terminal organelle (PubMed:2437033). The bulk of the protein is extracellular (PubMed:28671286)

The extracellular region has 2 domains; the N-terminus (approximately residues 59-1243) is a 7-bladed beta-propeller where the loops between the blades form a crown that projects away from the cell surface (PubMed:32513917). The stalk (approximately residues 1244-1346) links the N-terminus to the transmembrane helix (PubMed:32513917). The isolated C-terminus is quite different in structure from the same region in the whole extracellular domain, suggesting considerable domain plasticity (PubMed:32513917, PubMed:33135669). In both cryo-EM and cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) of the whole Nap complex a deep V is formed between the 2 heterodimers (PubMed:32513917, PubMed:37939157). Low resolution cryo-ET suggests 'open' and 'closed' conformations of the entire membrane-embedded complex where movements in the stalk region are amplified to open the crowns and allow ligand binding (PubMed:37939157). Sialylated oligosaccharides can be modeled in this entire Nap 'open' cryo-ET complex, where they might be stabilized by residues from this protein in addition to already characterized binding by P110 (Probable) (PubMed:37939157)

Not essential, it can be disrupted with no effect on short-term growth in vitro (PubMed:16407165). Cells clump and do not adhere to cell culture plastic surfaces, nor to erythrocytes (PubMed:17028283, PubMed:29470847). Cells no longer have the typical flask-shape and have lost the attachment organelle, most are round, about 23% are multilobed or pleomorphic (PubMed:17028283). Cells are not mobile, but assemble more than 2 electron dense complexes that underlie the attachment organelle (PubMed:29470847). Greatly decreased expression of P110 (mgpC), increased expression of DnaK and another unidentified protein, decreased expression of MG368 (PubMed:17028283)
Populations of M.genitalium unable to adhere to host cells express little to no P140 protein as well as another 94.7 kDa protein. Revertants able to adhere to host cells express these proteins again

4% of the genome of this strain encodes 9 partial copies of the major adhesion complex (MgPa repeats), variable repeated DNA elements which provide a pool of sequence variation for genes encoding the bacterial surface proteins (PubMed:8524858, PubMed:16790744). Sequence variation of the mgpB gene can be achieved by homologous, probably reciprocal, recombination between the repeated elements located within its ORF and the 9 repeat elements at other sites in the bacterial genome; this variation can be seen during culture in the laboratory (PubMed:16790744, PubMed:17880423). In samples taken from a single infected human patient over 21 months, 17 different mgpB variants were observed, showing mgpB intrastrain heterogeneity occurs in vivo during infection (PubMed:16790744)
Belongs to the adhesin P1 family
The original gene name was mgpA (PubMed:7569993); this has fallen into disuse and mgpB is more commonly used (PubMed:16790744, PubMed:26381903)

features.description: No change in adhesion to human red blood cells (hRBC). Loss of hRBC adhesion; when associated with 'F-947--951-F' and 'F-960--964-F' in P110, cells still assemble Nap complex, have multiple attachment organelles.
